lesson_title: Why Every Roller Coaster Hill Gets Smaller
hook_text: Look at any roller coaster: the first hill is always the tallest. That is not design taste, it is the law.
clip_script: The chain drags you up the first hill: electrical energy becomes height energy. Over the top, height becomes speed, and you scream. Up the next hill, speed becomes height again. So why can the second hill not be just as tall? Because the wheels rub on the track and the air shoves against you. Every metre, a little energy turns into heat and that roaring sound. It is not destroyed, energy never is, but it can no longer lift you. Lose enough, and a taller hill would leave you stuck. That is the law of conservation of energy: energy cannot be made or destroyed, only changed. And it is why nobody has ever built a machine that runs forever.
visual_style: Whiteboard side view of a roller coaster with hills shrinking left to right, a bar chart beside the car showing height energy, speed energy and a growing heat bar that always add to the same total.
pacing: Fast ride rhythm, a pause at the question, a firm finish on the law.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and balance any energy story.
